# Files API — local official npm 2.1.283 recovery

## 2026-10-04: bounded 287 header dependency integration

The retained 283 upload/download bodies now import `getFilesHeaders287 as zP`.
That dependency is the complete manifest-pinned 287 `H5t` plus
`cp/R/ewe/ZKr/gXo/hXo` closure, generated by
`scripts/official/files-headers-287.mjs`. The legacy recovery script and its
provenance explicitly record this dependency so regeneration does not revert it.
All other generated vendor files and retained native function bodies are unchanged.

The actual original public `--file` and bundle callers pass a session-ingress
token. This leaf does not choose a normal account OAuth token/API key or refresh
one after 401. Do not add such behavior based on the parameter's `oauthToken`
name. The existing UA/version owner stays at the product version until the 287
release gates pass; the original constant 287 UA is separately recorded.

The current public Files policy guard is bound through `filesPolicy287.ts` to the canonical ModelUsage/settings/provider/verified-remote owners. The earlier pending note was historical; accepted source evidence is in `pc-files-main-287-20261007`. No real account/server qualification is claimed.

`recover.mjs` checks the manifest version/platform and full module SHA-256 before
extracting complete declarations. `provenance.json` records the declaration and
generated-file hashes. Imports and the standalone host are adapted; original
function/class bodies in the generated JS are unchanged.

```sh
[private-reference-not-distributed] src/vendor/official-files-api/recover.mjs ../.work/official-modules-2.1.283/darwin-arm64
[private-reference-not-distributed] test tests/files-api-offline.test.ts
```

## Actual public consumption

`services/api/filesApi.ts` upload/download wrappers delegate to the original
functions. Local session batch/download-save consumers keep their existing
behavior. The pre-existing list implementation remains local; it now invokes
`x_` at entry, rather than silently bypassing the same egress boundary.

`loadPolicyLimits` -> actual Axios response -> extended `PolicyLimitsResponseSchema`
-> session/disk policy snapshot -> original `F4n` -> `oc` -> original Files `x_`.
The Files host also hydrates an existing local policy cache synchronously before
the gate. This performs **no auth discovery or network I/O**, even under the
existing local remote-prefetch opt-out. The opt-out itself is unchanged.

Taints-only responses persist, checksums include taints, 304/stale-fetch reuse
retains them, and state is applied before persistence. HTTP 404 / cache clear /
failed persistence never erase an already latched HIPAA denial. Only the explicit
test reset clears that latch. Normal restrictions retain their existing public
consumer (`isPolicyAllowed`); monitoring/defaults were not silently invented.

Uploads preserve: content override (including empty Buffer), timeout, signal,
`retryAfterTimeout`, expiration form field, purpose, byte length, basename
quote/CR/LF escaping, 500 MB check, categorized failure `reason`, three attempts
with 500/1000 ms backoff, and terminal 400/401/403/404/413/422/cancellation.
Original behavior matters: Axios-rejected 5xx exhaust as `network`, other retryable
statuses/missing IDs as `server`; direct ECONNABORTED only skips retries when
`retryAfterTimeout === false` and `cause === undefined`. Cancellation in backoff
stops the next dispatch but does not itself interrupt the original sleep.

Files still uses `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` and
`files-api-2025-04-14,oauth-2025-04-20`, independently of Messages headers.
No package, preload or tsconfig changes/dependencies are needed.

## Explicit remaining boundaries

- The whole policy identity-stamp admission/evidence broker, WIF/bearer attribution,
  cross-process HIPAA evidence store, held-start/verdict barrier, account-switch
  race defense, monitoring notice UI, defaults and remote gateway producer are
  **not restored by this change**. This is not enterprise compliance certification.
- Existing legacy policy cache consumption is retained. This host has no complete
  matched/torn/foreign identity-stamp protocol. It conservatively carries observed
  HIPAA taints across local cache/account clearing; missing/unsettled policy is
  not proof of eligibility. A fresh session with no recognized policy evidence
  follows the original Files `x_` predicate; it does not manufacture a server verdict.
- Gateway credential slots are genuine original state and tested, but their
  private gateway auth/server/policy producers are absent here. No gateway startup
  or private feature gate was enabled. Their deny contract is ready for a future
  real producer, not reported as an integrated gateway deployment.
- The entire policy service (eligibility, endpoint, retry/backoff and polling)
  remains the existing local host, with only real compliance schema/state/cache
  consumption added. Its two-field cache/checksum is not the official full
  monitoring/defaults/identity-stamp storage protocol.
- Real server account qualification, authentication and remote Files permissions
  were not tested. All validation uses isolated HOME, synthetic tokens, fake Axios
  adapters and a virtual backoff clock. No uploads, real model or external network.

## 287 Files policy/data production extension (2026-10-04)

`files.js` is now emitted by `scripts/official/files-data-287.mjs`: whole 287
upload/download functions, existing header owner, and `_He/D7e` via
`src/services/api/filesPolicy287.ts`. `recover.mjs` preserves that accepted output rather
than regenerating or overwriting it with 283. Other legacy compliance/issuer assets remain 283;
they are not the new Files provider guard owner. New source evidence is
`files287.provenance.json` and `officialFilesPolicy287/provenance.json`.

The source cut uses the existing ModelUsage policy selector, canonical settings
store, native provider/credential slots and verified remote owner. Verified versus
unverified pins and explicit denial are covered through actual upload. Machine
file/MDM reader provenance/native invalid-provider validation gap remains a specifically recorded
shared-source interface gap, not a claim of whole settings-source parity.
